newsitem.title: FRANCE: France appeals for end to violence in Serbia.
newsitem.headline: France appeals for end to violence in Serbia.

text.p: France appealed on Thursday for an end to violent confrontations in Yugoslavia between backers and foes of President Slobodan Milosevic and urged the Serbian authorities to ensure freedom of expression.
"This new cycle of violence must immediately be interrupted and those responsible for the violent incidents brought before the appropriate judicial authorities," a Foreign Ministry spokeswoman said.

"At the same time, we urge the Serbian government to commit itself to bringing the two sides together and to begin a dialogue based on the recommendations to be issued tomorrow by the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE)," the spokeswoman said.
The OSCE is expected to deliver its opinion on the outcome of November 17 local elections shortly.
Riot police intervened on Tuesday to separate clashing pro- and anti-government demonstrators who fought running skirmishes in the streets of Belgrade.
At least 58 people were injured in the melee, including one man who was shot and critically wounded by a Milosevic supporter.
The protests began after Milosevic and his ruling SPS party refused to accept a stunning series of opposition victories in the November 17 local elections.

Opposition protests had taken place without violence for more than five weeks until Milosevic and the SPS transported supporters from outside Belgrade into the city on Tuesday for a rally at the same time and place as the daily opposition march.
France strongly condemned the violence, saying it prevented a settlement of the crisis.
